text:
alex: FYI we're seeing intermittent 401s in the deploy pipeline since yesterday afternoon. only affects prod deploy job, staging is fine.

maria: seeing the same. failure window is around the long artifact upload step (~10-15m into job). job retries don't help.

kevin: logs from the runner show `token_expired` at the time of failure. attaching a snippet below.

kevin: ```
2026-02-14T18:12:03Z ci-runner: request POST /v1/models: 401 {
  "error": "invalid_token",
  "message": "service account impersonation token expired"
}
2026-02-14T18:12:03Z ci-runner: retry 1 -> create_impersonated_token() returned 401
```

anna: quick context: deploy uses GitHub Actions OIDC to mint a short-lived token that the CI runner then uses to impersonate the `deploy-bot@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com`. Impersonation was configured with max TTL 1h but the intermediate credential from GH is 5m.

alex: interesting — the failure correlates with long artifact upload. maybe the impersonated token is created at the start and then expires mid-job.

maria: confirmed: runner workflow calls `gcloud iam service-accounts generate-access-token --impersonate-service-account=deploy-bot@... --duration=3600s` at job start, but GH OIDC audience token presented to STS can only be exchanged for a short-lived credential, and our ephemeral refresh logic doesn't re-run until the next step, so token stale.

kevin: repro steps I used locally:
1) start a job that sleeps 1000s after token issue (`sleep 1000`)
2) run the upload step that uses GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN issued at job start
3) observe 401 during upload after ~5-10m

kevin: curl to the API during repro: 
```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/predict -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -v
# -> HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
# {"error":"invalid_token","details":"token expired"}
```

maria: root cause seems to be TTL mismatch between OIDC-issued token and the impersonation session. also we have no in-job refresh for long-running steps.

devops-bot: @channel Incident preliminary triage recorded. ticket ID INC-2026-022. Audit log links: https://console.cloud.google.com/logs/query; action: serviceAccountTokens.create (deploy-bot).

anna: Proposed mitigations:
- short term (hotfix): update runner to refresh impersonated token before long blocking steps (add a pre-upload refresh). add a small retry wrapper around upload with token refresh on 401.
- medium term: change GH workflow to request a token closer to the upload step (move generate-access-token step later), or break the long step into smaller chunks.
- long term: implement automatic token introspection + background refresh in the CI runner (detect expiry and re-impersonate).

kevin: security note: the impersonated role currently has overly broad perms (Editor). we should scope to the minimal permissions required: storage.objects.create, storage.objects.get, storage.objects.delete and the specific model-inference API write perms.

maria: agreed. we should rotate from broad service account to two dedicated service accounts: one for artifact storage (scoped to GCS) and one for deploy actions (scoped to model/admin but least privilege). then use cloud IAM bindings to limit who can impersonate each.

alex: quick config I tested that alleviates repro locally: call `gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=...` right before the upload step and export to GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN. cuts failures to zero in my runs.

kevin: here's a minimal retry snippet we can add to the runner bash: 
```bash
function upload_with_refresh() {
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    RESULT=$(upload_cmd) && return 0
    # on 401 refresh token and retry
    if [[ "$RESULT" == *"401"* ]]; then
      echo "refreshing token..."
      export GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=$IMPERSONATE_SA)
      sleep 1
      continue
    fi
    sleep $((i*2))
  done
  return 1
}
```

anna: follow-ups I'm putting on the ticket:
- [ ] add job-level token refresh step (short term)
- [ ] create two least-privilege SAs and update workflows (medium)
- [ ] update runner to support background token refresh (long)
- [ ] add CI-side metric: token age at request time -> help detect future regressions

maria: also flagging a monitoring alert: add a 401-rate alert on deploy pipelines so we catch regressions before they become customer-facing.

alex: one more edge: clock skew can cause premature expiry if runners have time drift. confirm NTP sync on fleet. kevin can you check runner host time?

kevin: checking now. one problematic runner had ~120s drift; fixed with ntp syncd restart. I pushed a tiny change to our runner image to ensure chrony is running.

devops-bot: deploy pipeline status: next run scheduled at 18:40 UTC with temp hotfix changes (refresh before upload). CI run link: https://ci.redwood.inference/runs/34567

audit-bot: recorded permission change suggestion in audit: change deploy-bot role from Editor -> roles/storage.objectAdmin + custom model-invoke role.

anna: I'll draft the PR to split SAs and update the workflows. assigning to @maria and @kevin for review.

maria: thanks. I'll also open a small runbook entry under docs/ci (#internal) explaining token TTL pitfalls and the recommended pattern for long-running jobs.

kevin: implementing hotfix now and will monitor. will post a follow-up when the next run completes.

alex: thanks everyone. main takeaways: TTL mismatch + long-running step + occasional host clock skew. mitigation path clear. :thumbsup:
